newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO REACH THIRD ROUND DESPITE HOME DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO REACH THIRD ROUND DESPITE HOME DEFEAT.

text.p: Monaco went down 1-0 to Borussia Moenchengladbach in a dull match on Tuesday but still qualified comfortably for the third round of the UEFA Cup through their 4-2 win in Germany in the first leg.
Moenchengladbach, needing at least three goals to qualify, pushed forward in the first half but never really worried a tight Monaco defence.
Monaco, playing cautiously before their home fans, did not show much initiative until the 44th minute when Brazilian Anderson set up Victor Ikpeba with a superb pass.
The Nigerian striker beat Borussia goalkeeper Uwe Kamps from close range but the goal was disallowed for an off-side which did not look obvious on television replays.

Feeling that they had little to fear, Monaco dropped their guard slightly after the break and Moenchengladbach managed to score in the 70th minute through an acrobatic volley from inside the penalty area by Michael Klinkert.
Monaco pressed in the last minutes but several brilliant saves by Kamps prevented an equaliser.
In their next match, Monaco will be without Scottish midfielder John Collins who received his second booking in this season's competition.
